title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in E420 Euler recasts the calculus of variations with an auxiliary parameter. In the second part, on surfaces, the ordinate z is treated as a function z(x,y,t). A 'variation' is the increment produced by changing t alone, with dx = dy = 0. On the previous page he fixed notation: p, p' are the first partials of z in x and y; q, q', q'' the second partials; r, r', r'', r''' the third partials; s, ... the fourth. He also wrote the total differential of an arbitrary 'expression of the second kind' V(x,y,z,p,p',q,q',q'',r,...) as dV = L dx + M dy + N dz + P dp + P' dp' + Q dq + ... + R''' dr'''.

This page (§22, continued) gives the variations of the derivative variables at fixed (x,y). Since partial derivatives commute:
- δp = dt ∂²z/∂x∂t and δp' = dt ∂²z/∂y∂t;
- δq = dt ∂³z/∂x²∂t, δq' = dt ∂³z/∂x∂y∂t, δq'' = dt ∂³z/∂y²∂t;
- δr = dt ∂⁴z/∂x³∂t, and so on up to δr''' = dt ∂⁴z/∂y³∂t.

§23: substituting into dV with dx = dy = 0 and dropping the common factor dt gives
∂V/∂t = N z_t + P z_{xt} + P' z_{yt} + Q z_{xxt} + Q' z_{xyt} + Q'' z_{yyt} + R z_{xxxt} + R' z_{xxyt} + R'' z_{xyyt} + R''' z_{yyyt}.
This is the first variation (Gateaux derivative along the family) of a pointwise function of the jet of z. It suffices for all 'expressions of the second kind'.

§24 opens the 'third kind': expressions involving integrals. The next page shows these are double integrals ∫∫V dx dy over a base region, as in surface extremum problems. There Euler refers to Novi Comm. XIV for double integrals.
errors: Printing slip: dp' = dt(dp'/dt) = (ddz/dy dt) omits the factor dt on the right-hand side; it should be dt(ddz/dy dt).
Printing slip in the R'' term of §23: 'd x a y² d t' should be 'dx dy² dt'.

The text says 'quarumcunque expressionum secundi generis', but only terms up to third-order derivatives of z (fourth-order mixed with t) are written. The rest is implied by 'etc.'; this is not an error, only a truncation.

ideas.what: Representing a variation by embedding the unknown function in a one-parameter family z(x,y,t) and differentiating partially in t at fixed x,y
ideas.modern_name: First variation as a Gateaux/directional derivative along a one-parameter family
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, E420 (1771/1772) and the companion papers E385/E386 on the variational method (as discussed by Fraser and Goldstine); the δ-algorithm itself is Lagrange 1755/1760
ideas.where_published: E420 (Novi Comm. 16); the single-variable version is earlier in the same paper; E385/E386 also treat the δ-method

ideas.what: Commutation of variation with partial differentiation: δ(∂^k z/∂x^i∂y^j) = ∂^k(δz)/∂x^i∂y^j
ideas.modern_name: Commuting δ with d (equality of mixed partials)
ideas.where_published: E420 and earlier Euler and Lagrange variational papers

ideas.what: Chain-rule formula for the variation of a function of the jet of z(x,y)
ideas.modern_name: Linearization of a Lagrangian density on the jet bundle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange 1760 (minimal surface), Euler E420 in general form

ideas.what: Announcement of double-integral functionals ∫∫V dx dy for surface extremum problems, with a reference to the earlier treatment of double integrals
ideas.modern_name: Multiple-integral calculus of variations; Fubini-type iterated integration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange 1760 (minimal surfaces); Euler E391 (double integrals, Novi Comm. 14)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine notational step: chain-rule substitution of t-variations of partial derivatives, in the well-known Euler parameter method for surface variational problems. The paper is well studied in histories of the calculus of variations.
transcription_corrections: The original itself lacks the dt in 'dp' = dt(dp'/dt) = (ddz/dy dt)'; the transcription faithfully reproduces this slip of the print.
The R'' term in §23 is printed 'd x a y² d t' in the original. The transcription silently normalizes it to dx dy² dt.
